name: Holt & Rein Melton Overcoat
description:
A knee-length overcoat in midnight navy boiled wool melton, structured and clean-lined with a hidden placket, welt pockets, and a back vent that sits perfectly flat. Holt & Rein is a Tier 4 heritage label — not flashy, not technological, just extraordinarily well-made traditional tailoring. The shoulders are canvas-padded, the chest is half-lined in silk-analogue charmeuse, and the collar rolls with a softness that takes a skilled block-presser to achieve. Every coat is cut by hand in their Spire-adjacent atelier.

This is the coat of senior analysts, mid-level corponation liaisons, and the kind of Tier 3 professional who saved up for something that will outlast their career. It communicates seriousness without aggression, authority without ostentation. On the street, it reads as expensive to anyone who knows fabric. To those who don't, it just reads as correct.
what_it_says: You have good taste and the patience to find it. You are not someone who needs to announce themselves.
story_hooks: A Holt & Rein overcoat left at a crime scene belongs to a registered identity that doesn't match any living person — the coat is three years old but the identity was created six months ago.
The label inside all Holt & Rein coats contains a serial number traceable to the specific tailor who cut it — someone is using this to track a person they believe is still alive.
A Tier 2 character inherits one of these coats from a dead relative and finds that wearing it opens doors — people assume they belong in rooms they've never entered before.

physical_description.visual_profile: A commanding knee-length overcoat with a refined, almost military bearing. The silhouette is vertical and authoritative—broad canvas-padded shoulders taper to a clean waist, creating a subtle hourglass. The coat sits with architectural precision, neither stiff nor relaxed. On the wearer, it projects quiet competence and understated rank.
physical_description.fit: Tailored with controlled ease through the body—not slim, not oversized. Allows layering beneath without bunching. The back vent maintains a flat, unbroken line when standing; subtle A-line when moving. Sleeve length hits mid-hand. Cut for someone who moves with intention.
physical_description.primary_material: Midnight navy boiled wool melton—dense, water-resistant, and hand-finished. The fabric has weight and substance without bulk. Surface shows subtle nap variation depending on light direction.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost satin-like from the boiling process, with a barely-perceptible nap. Charmeuse silk-analogue half-lining whispers against skin. The wool itself feels compact and stable, not fuzzy—evidence of skilled finishing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep midnight navy that absorbs light rather than reflects it. No patterns. Tonal charmeuse lining glimpsed at the chest. Subtle contrast stitching in darker thread.
physical_description.closures: Hidden placket conceals a row of hand-finished horn buttons (matte charcoal). Magnetic snaps reinforce the closure invisibly. No visible fasteners contribute to the seamless front plane.
distinctive_features: Hand-cut construction—subtle irregularities in seam placement that signal bespoke work
Canvas-padded shoulders with soft roll, not rigid structure
Welt pockets positioned for proportion, not function
Back vent sits flat with precision pressing
Half-silk-analogue lining in charmeuse—luxury visible only to the wearer
Soft, carefully-rolled collar with hand-block pressing
Interior maker's label: Holt & Rein, Spire atelier designation
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 boundary. Accessible to disciplined professionals; unattainable to sub-grade workers. No Φ symbol or tech integration signals old-money sensibility in a future-forward world.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by corporate analysts who've earned seniority without aug-splurging, liaisons who need to move between high and mid-tier spaces, academics, and archivists. The wearer is someone who invests in durability over display. Signals restraint, competence, and financial security through understatement.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. The wool develops a soft patina with wear—slight color deepening at stress points (sleeves, button stance), polished creases that sharpen rather than crease. A well-worn Holt & Rein coat looks more expensive than a new one.

image_prompt: Overhead 3/4 shot of a midnight navy wool melton overcoat draped over a dark chrome mannequin, positioned in a brutalist concrete atelier space. Soft diffused window light catches the nap of the fabric, revealing subtle sheen variations. The collar is hand-pressed with visible softness; the back vent is geometrically flat. One welt pocket is slightly open, revealing silk-analogue charmeuse lining in charcoal. Fine details: horn button closure peeking from hidden placket, crisp stitching, canvas shoulder structure visible in silhouette. Background: industrial shelving, fabric swatches, pressing blocks.
